facts: Petitioners are Administrative Officer Grade II and Finance Officer who claim special pay as given to their counter-parts drawn from the Secretariat Service.
Their claim was negatived by Ext. P2 order dated 7th January 1981.

They approached this court for quashing Ext. P2 order and for the issue of a writ of mandamus directing the Government to grant the petitioners special pay as in the case of their counterparts in the Secretariat service.

The learned Single Judge dismissed the Original Petition holding that the special pay is given to a class or persons by reason of the special nature of their work and so it is based on a reasonable classification.
issues: Whether the action of the Government in granting the special pay to Administrative Officers/Finance Officers/Financial Assistants drawn from the Secretariat wing alone is illegal, discriminatory and violative of the principles contained in Articles 14 and 16 of the Constitution.
Whether officers like the petitioners who belong to the same cadre but are not drawn from the Secretariat are denied the benefit of special pay.
petitioner_arguments: The action of the Government in granting the special pay to Administrative Officers/Finance Officers/Financial Assistants drawn from the Secretariat wing alone is illegal, discriminatory and violative of the principles contained in Articles 14 and 16 of the Constitution.
Officers like the petitioners who belong to the same cadre but are not drawn from the Secretariat are denied the benefit of special pay.
respondent_arguments: The reason for the said treatment is explained in paragraph 5 of the counter affidavit: 'Normally a Secretariat Officer is not expected to be transferred and posted for work in the offices of Heads of Departments.'
court_reasoning: The Supreme Court in M. P. Singh v. The Union of India had considered the validity of special pay given to certain C.B.I. Officers on account of the arduous nature of their duties.
Article 39(d) of the Constitution provides that the State shall direct its policy towards securing equal pay for equal work for both men and women.

When it is admitted that persons belonging to one cadre are discharging the same functions, duties and responsibilities, the State will not be justified in granting special pay to a group of them depending on the source from which they are drawn.
holding: We declare that the appellants are entitled to the Special Pay, like their counter-parts drawn from the Secretariat Service.
The decision of the learned Single Judge to the contrary is unsustainable in view of the decisions of the Supreme Court, referred to hereinabove.
